extracted.intended_audience: educators, administrators, and project directors preparing proposals to the Florida Division of Vocational Education (state/federal vocational funding applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, writing, submitting, and managing proposals seeking vocational education funding (preliminary and final proposals) to the Division of Vocational Education; includes proposal components, evaluation criteria, and post-award project management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Statement (description + rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem statement includes a description of the problem as well as the rationale for the project. It should state the problem and its significance to vocational education in clear, concise terms and include both present conditions and desired conditions so that the discrepancy between them, the problem, is made obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must convince the funding agency that the problem is important and the proposed solution appropriate and likely to contribute to vocational education. Include: (1) problem description, (2) importance of the problem, (3) its relationship to vocational education, (4) the rationale/justification for the project. Keep limited in scope so it is solvable; provide background, observed conditions, documentation where possible, and note transportability/generalizability if applicable. Examples and a sample problem statement (Gulfside drafting example) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Description: gap/documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem is a need identified as a gap or discrepancy between the present (what is) and the ideal (what should be).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe present and desired conditions (e.g., chart 'WHAT IS / WHAT SHOULD BE'); document discrepancies when possible (enrollment figures, labor market data, needs surveys). Distinguish mere observation from documented need and limit the problem to a solvable scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A needs assessment is a formalized search for information (usually by survey) attempting to identify discrepancies between what is and what should be; it is the search for the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two approaches: broad exploratory surveys to reveal previously unknown problems, or directed surveys to investigate a known problem's causes and extent. Collect information on what has already been tried locally and related programs; where possible gather quantifiable data to justify need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / Rationale for Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale provides the basis for funding — a justification explaining why the problem is important and why the proposed solution is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the extent (local/regional/state/national), impact on target groups, implications if unmet, and potential for results to be disseminated or transported. Show how the project will address community/industry needs and broader applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Present background information relevant to the problem statement and review pertinent studies which provide a foundation for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select studies that mark important points; balance between exhaustive reporting and neglect. Describe studies briefly with enough detail to show relevance and how the proposed study moves beyond them. Use past tense for completed studies; present tense for ongoing studies. Define unfamiliar terms. Relate the review explicitly to the proposed study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (WHAT IS TO BE ACCOMPLISHED)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives are statements of what is to be accomplished. Each objective should be a simple sentence describing the outcome to be achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin objectives with action verbs (e.g., develop, evaluate, train, prepare). Each objective should include: (1) an ACTION verb, (2) WHAT outcome is to be accomplished, (3) WHEN or time span, (4) what CRITERIA are to be used in measuring accomplishment and under what conditions. Use only one major measurable item per objective; make objectives specific, achievable, measurable, and ordered by importance. Examples illustrate unsatisfactory vs. satisfactory objectives and condensed measurable forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (overall: HOW IT WILL BE CONDUCTED)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology explains how the project will be conducted, including procedures and organizational/administrative arrangements (project management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit details to convince reviewers objectives can be accomplished. Use a planning grid linking problem → objectives → methods → evaluation to check alignment. Include the following subcomponents (participants, setting, facilities/equipment, supplies/materials, staffing, timeline, data collection/analysis, evaluation, dissemination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (sampling & eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe persons who will be affected/measured by the project (subjects/population/sample), their number, and eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State characteristics (age, education level, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, program participation, sex) and any generalizability limits. Explain selection method (random, stratified, cluster, intact units) and rationale. Reviewers expect to know who is selected, how, and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (appropriateness & demographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting in which the project will be conducted (districts, communities, schools, classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide demographic characteristics useful for reviewers to assess appropriateness and generalization of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe special facilities or equipment required to accomplish objectives and the rationale for acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate method and criteria used to select and acquire facilities/equipment; note cooperative arrangements as alternatives to purchase/rental. Note that approval for equipment purchases/facility rental is the exception; proposals with little or no equipment purchases have a better chance of funding. Describe libraries, offices, or special facilities and their selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify consumable supplies and materials necessary for the project (paper, filmstrips, tapes, textbooks, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details need not appear in the narrative but are required for the budget. Distinguish supplies (consumables) and materials (non-consumables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing (personnel qualifications & time commitment)
rubrics_metrics.description: List all personnel positions required for administering the project, ensuring number and qualifications are realistic for attaining objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include titles (project director, secretary, consultants), assignment descriptions, percentage of time committed. Name a project director responsible for administration, final report, and products; include brief qualifications in appendix if identified. Make staffing realistic for scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Schedule / Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a feasible schedule including times for major activities, administration, and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines should show that the project can be completed in a reasonable amount of time. Objectives should include time spans. Reviewers check feasibility of schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Collection and Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods for collecting and analyzing data to assess project outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify instruments, administration timing (pre/post as applicable), sampling, statistical significance criteria (example: .05 level), and how measures relate to objectives. Ensure analysis methods are appropriate to answer evaluation questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (process & criteria of success)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an evaluation plan indicating how success will be measured and by what criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include formative and summative evaluation procedures, specific measures tied to objectives, criteria of acceptable success (e.g., 30% gain among 2/3 of students), responsible parties for evaluation, and plans for monitoring project progress. Project monitors may provide continuing evaluation after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination (results/products use and distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how results and products will be communicated and to whom, and potential uses of outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List target audiences (guidance counselors, teachers, administrators), planned articles or presentations (e.g., submit to Florida Vocational Journal), and how products will be made available. Outcomes should be clearly described and be a logical outgrowth of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget (itemization & realism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget must be itemized, complete, and realistic in relation to objectives, procedures, and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for purchases/rentals; avoid large equipment/facility budgets where possible; align budget line-items with project needs and objectives. Reviewers check whether budget is realistic to achieve stated results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Format and Submission (use official form and signatures)
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must be submitted on the proposal form found in the Application for Federal Vocational Funds and completed in accordance with its instruction manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all items apply to every category—enter NA where not applicable. Proposal submissions: part of annual plan or as amendments; required signatures include superintendent or college/university president; one copy of the preliminary proposal form is required initially; follow instructions for copies and addresses (mail to Division unless specified). RFP responses should note RFP identification number on preliminary proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Scope and Manageability
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep projects limited in scope so they are workable and can be completed within reasonable time and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fewer well-focused objectives are preferable to many broad objectives; scope must match available resources and timeframe. Avoid overly broad problem statements that indicate lack of focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / Exemplary Qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: For Innovative or Exemplary projects, procedures should be unique or original in approach and application, or represent an exemplary program that can be studied as a successful technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exemplary program should be creative, imaginative, and combine elements unique in method or technique. For innovation, show originality and potential to serve as model or example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex Equity / Non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs must comply with assurances of non-discrimination on the basis of sex; projects should be available and easily accessible to persons of either sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for neutral language, objectives free of sex bias and stereotyping, documented availability/accessibility (special services or support services to ensure equal access), and evaluation data collection to substantiate elimination of sex bias. Projects may be designed to overcome sex bias via curriculum adjustments, nontraditional job preparation, inservice training, or other services. A project may be recommended but will not be funded until sex-equity items are satisfactorily addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Review Criteria (Proposal Review Form elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal reviewers will evaluate specific elements using the Proposal Evaluation Form, including Nature of the Problem, Purpose and Objectives, Procedures, Outcomes/Products, Budget, and Other Factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific reviewer questions include: Does proposal adequately describe the need and present evidence? Will solution impact vocational education? Do purpose and objectives reflect understanding and are objectives specific, measurable, concrete, achievable, relevant? Are procedures definite, logical, complete, and adequate? For innovation: is the procedure unique or studyable as exemplary? Are outcomes/products clearly described and logically resulting from project? Is budget itemized and realistic? Other factors include sex equity and whether project will contribute to solution. Maximum points per element are listed on the official evaluation form (subject to revision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Administrative/Post-Award Requirements (project management)
rubrics_metrics.description: After award, project implementation procedures include copyright clearance, project monitoring and evaluation, project amendment procedures, final report writing, and product description/dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project director must follow implementation steps: secure copyright clearance for products as needed, cooperate with project monitors for continuing evaluation, submit amendments if project scope or budget changes, prepare and submit final reports, and provide product descriptions for dissemination. Division may assist with dissemination and production services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Proposal / RFP Response Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary proposals use the preliminary proposal form in the Application for Federal Vocational Funds and may be submitted as part of the annual plan or as an amendment; RFPs require responses on the preliminary proposal form and must include the RFP identification number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary proposals are abbreviated but should reflect careful planning and understanding of full proposal components. Preliminary proposals are reviewed by advisory councils and administrative council; invited applicants submit final proposals with requested modifications and required number of copies.
